commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reduce encoder graph fallback staging and audio metadata overhead after #68831, while preserving compact cached output storage. Capture limits, including the default **5,120 encoder tokens**, remain unchanged.

## Motivation

The [review benchmarks](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68831#issuecomment-7056172375) found that enabling encoder graphs could slow down batches outside the captured range. The manager still sorted/concatenated inputs and cloned outputs per item. Returning batch-backed eager views would reduce that cost but let one cached item retain an entire batch. Short clips can exceed the item limit well below 5K tokens.

This follows up the merged PR: bypass unnecessary staging, compact only outputs with excess backing storage, batch the required allocations/copy, and remove repeated frontend/attention metadata work. Triton audio attention recomputed identical window lengths in each of the 18/32 encoder layers; it now computes them once per forward, including each graph replay.

## Claims

- The Qwen3 audio mixin opts into an internal fast path for whole-batch eager fallback: preserve input order, skip graph selection/concatenation, reuse compact outputs and compact oversized backing storage with `torch._foreach_clone`. Its default `False` leaves other encoders on their existing sorting, staging and postprocessing policy.
- CPU integer/NumPy bookkeeping and batched CUDA padding reduce audio frontend launches. Equal chunks use one packed copy; CUDA batches of at least 32 varied chunks use a zero-sentinel gather. Smaller varied batches and non-CUDA devices retain sequence padding.
- NVIDIA Triton audio forwards reuse one window-length tensor across layers. The optional attention argument retains the existing recomputation when omitted. No new capture buffers or user-facing settings/default changes.

## Validation

Runtime validated at `0dd3188c12`; final head `3553b262bf` differs only in documentation, docstrings and tests (executable code unchanged); comparison base **main `dd8c157895`**. GB200, BF16, TRITON_ATTN, TP=1. Full public ASR-0.6B audio architecture (18×896) and Omni-30B-A3B audio architecture (32×1280), held seeded random weights and synthetic mel inputs. Model/batch token limits 8,192, max sequences 128, default auto graph budgets capped at **5,120**, auto item limit 78, 34 graphs.

| Model | All 30 cases vs main + graphs | 14 fallbacks vs main eager |
|---|---:|---:|
| ASR | 6.5–20.2% faster | 4.2–16.6% faster |
| OMNI | 4.8–15.4% faster | 4.0–12.7% faster |

These are **encoder-stage wall latencies**, including CNN, host metadata, sorting/staging/copies, transformer/projection, output handling and GPU completion. Feature extraction, decoder/serving queues, capture and JIT are outside the timed region. Each model's full run has 30 workloads, **72 samples per arm**, 12 warmups, three rotating inputs. One GPU workload runs at a time on GPU0 with CPUs 20–23. Each complete block contains all 24 permutations of four arms, shuffled and repeated three times, so every arm occupies every position equally. The fresh critical-case repeats add an identical main-eager arm as an ordering/noise control (largest observed median difference 0.50%).

| Workload | Tokens | ASR: main graphs / main eager → PR (ms) | Omni: main graphs / main eager → PR (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 short clips | 416 | 2.559 / 9.218 → 2.222 | 3.776 / 16.852 → 3.409 |
| One long clip | 1,664 | 4.726 / 9.658 → 4.001 | 6.639 / 15.892 → 5.876 |
| Long + 16 short clips | 1,768 | 5.044 / 9.908 → 4.274 | 7.105 / 15.976 → 6.281 |

| 128 short clips | 1,664 | 12.057 / 10.302 → 9.627 | 18.056 / 16.280 → 15.280 |

The baselines remain fixed main controls. **Within the patched version**, graph-enabled fallback remains up to **4.1% slower than graphs-disabled eager** because the graphs-disabled path returns batch-backed views while fallback compacts cache outputs. The table does not claim zero overhead when toggling the feature in the patched version.

The former small-regression cases and 128-item boundary were also rerun in fresh processes with **240 samples/arm**, two complete permutation blocks, at the same final source:

IQRs describe within-run spread; the two process runs are reported separately rather than presented as a confidence interval.

### Memory and output correctness

| Fallback | ASR main → PR extra peak (MiB) | Omni main → PR extra peak (MiB) |
|---|---:|---:|
| one_above_cap | 2953.21 → 2943.45 | 2953.21 → 2943.45 |
| mixed_above_cap | 2953.60 → 2943.84 | 2953.21 → 2943.45 |
| 96_short_item_overflow | 711.78 → 709.43 | 712.40 → 710.05 |
| 96_varied_short_overflow | 1183.30 → 1179.75 | 1182.77 → 1179.75 |
| 128_short_item_overflow | 948.97 → 945.84 | 949.91 → 946.78 |

These are peak additional `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` bytes above each call's starting allocation, after warmup; resident weights and graph pools are excluded. No tested audio case increases this peak versus the main manager. Retained non-DP fallback outputs have backing storage no larger than their logical bytes, including after sibling cache eviction. Tests also retain outputs across subsequent replays.

All tested fallback outputs are bitwise equal to original-order main eager. Replay outputs are bitwise equal to main replay and checked against eager on identical padded buffers. Padding/order-dependent BF16 differences already present in main are recorded separately; the benchmark does not widen the output tolerance to hide them.

- Encoder suite plus attention-wrapper tests: **167 passed, 1 warning in 86.15s (0:01:26)**. Permanent test additions are limited to extending the existing overflow test (order, replay lifetime and per-item storage) and checking the optional custom-op argument in the existing fake-layout test: 16 added / 6 removed lines, no new test functions or fixtures.
- Real pretrained ASR through `LLM`, two audio assets, 64 greedy tokens/top-5 logprobs with encoder graphs off/on, explicit Triton encoder/decoder and a 512 MiB KV budget (local validation only): **passed** with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.
- Negative control: disabling fallback output compaction fails the two multi-item storage assertions; the singleton case remains valid. Detailed padding oracles, kernel profiles and workload sweeps are retained as local validation rather than additional permanent tests.
- Local two-layer Triton capture/eager/replay probes checked cross-layer length storage reuse and rejected forced per-layer recomputation. These are validation evidence, not extra CI test functions; the executable code is unchanged from that probed revision.
- Real constructed reduced-width BF16 transformers with 18/32 layers: actual CUDA profiler shows **18→1 / 32→1** length-subtraction kernels, with exact old/new outputs. This is a kernel-count/correctness check, not the full-width latency result above.
- CPU integer-formula parity, FP32/BF16 frontend/forward parity, real reduced Step3-VL compact-output reuse, and two-rank reduced Qwen3-VL replay/mixed/overflow/empty-shard checks pass. DP's final gather retains its existing shared-output layout.
- Full commit hooks pass, including mypy, formatting, docstrings and test tethering. AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, validation and this description.

### Shared vision path

Full Qwen3-VL-2B vision architecture, random weights, unused decoder reduced, synthetic packed uint8 patches; same encoder/attention implementation in both arms to isolate the manager. 72 samples/arm, 8 warmups, all six arm-order permutations repeated equally. The graph replay case below 4,224 tokens already runs slower than graphs-disabled eager in main; this PR preserves that replay policy. The 5K cap is a coverage/memory tradeoff, not a guarantee that replay beats eager on every model/shape.

| Shared-manager vision control | Tokens/items | Main manager → PR manager (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| one_small | 49/1 | 1.965 → 1.975 |
| 32_small | 1568/32 | 13.829 → 13.826 |
| one_below_token_cap | 4096/1 | 90.487 → 90.716 |
| one_large | 5184/1 | 116.891 → 116.905 |
| mixed_large | 5169/3 | 83.992 → 84.019 |
| item_overflow | 4704/96 | 22.221 → 22.244 |

Reported gains cover this GB200/Triton configuration. Full serving throughput, corpus WER, other hardware and local FlashAttention performance remain outside this validation.

## Details

The internal fast-path opt-in is enabled only by the Qwen3 audio mixin. Early bypass applies when overflow is known before item selection; other encoders keep their established selection and output policy, including vision load balancing. Late capture-axis/replay-capacity misses retain existing staging/copy behavior. Mixed eager/replay paths and DP gathering are unchanged.

The shared slicing utility is unchanged from main. Compaction uses CPU storage metadata and reuses already compact custom postprocessor outputs. The audio length identities and padding keep the old CNN values/layout. Triton length reuse is local to each forward, so capture warmup cannot leave a stale cached tensor for later replay.

Duplicate-work checks include #68831 backlinks, encoder eager staging/cache storage, audio padding and Triton sequence-length searches. #62494 partially overlaps the gather idea in an older quantization/host-sync rewrite; it does not cover graph fallback staging, bounded batched output compaction or per-forward Triton metadata reuse. This implementation keeps the existing CPU-length contract and CNN layout and measures uniform/small/large varied batches. #63822 addresses generic cache/arena compaction; this change preserves manager-local bounded storage and removes execution overhead. #68083/#68066 address FlashInfer metadata/layout. These goals do not replace their remaining work.
